# omx-dsp / fuzz_src

omx-dsp's own fuzz target `fuzz_src` ([source](source/fuzz_src.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over omx-dsp 0.27.0 (FreeMixer/omx-dsp at a0ee1dfe).

Reads a source and destination rate as any 32-bit words and asks for a conversion plan; when the plan is refused, the run ends there. Otherwise it designs the polyphase table and reads up to 16 blocks of finite samples, 0 to 512 each. It converts the take twice: once in a single call, and once either whole or cut into the blocks the input gave, with or without a final flush. The two outputs, the plan and the table are then checked.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against libomxdsp.a, which build.sh compiles from omx-dsp's five src/*.c files with -DOMX_CONTRACTS and -ffp-contract=off; the converter is inline in omx_src.h. The Makefile's own fuzz build uses native clang with libFuzzer, which this build replaces with the standard driver.
- omx-contract's headers are pinned to the tag v3.4.0 (1169c701), where the library's Makefile uses whichever omx-contract is installed, at or above its packaging floor of 3.1.0.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- The plan is refused exactly when a rate is 0 or the reduced interpolation factor (computed with the harness's own gcd) exceeds the limit ([lines 86-101](source/fuzz_src.c#L86-L101)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The plan is the reduced ratio: gcd(l, m) is 1 and l times the source rate equals m times the destination rate ([lines 102-115](source/fuzz_src.c#L102-L115)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The take run in the blocks the input gives yields the same samples, bit for bit and in the same count, as the take run whole ([lines 152-158](source/fuzz_src.c#L152-L158)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Without a flush, no more samples come out than a whole file's frames plus half the filter length. No take makes more samples than the capacity of what went in ([lines 160-175](source/fuzz_src.c#L160-L175)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Every output is finite and no larger than the input's peak times the table's worst per-phase absolute coefficient sum ([lines 176-184](source/fuzz_src.c#L176-L184)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- An identity plan returns the input samples unchanged ([lines 185-192](source/fuzz_src.c#L185-L192)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The coefficients of each phase of the table sum to 1, to within 1e-4 ([lines 196-203](source/fuzz_src.c#L196-L203)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- At the end of the conversion, no contract of the library is recorded as broken. The converter states no contracts, so nothing on this path records one and the check cannot fail ([lines 160-168](source/fuzz.h#L160-L168)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
